q: The air flow moving above the top curved surface of the wing has a longer distance to travel and needs to go faster to have the same transit time as the air travelling along the lower flat surface.
e: True. The air flow moving above the top curved surface of the wing has a longer distance to travel and needs to go faster to have the same transit time as the air travelling. Faster air over the longer top path lowers pressure there and lift appears.

q: The velocity of air flow is low along the top surface and high along the bottom surface of an aeroplane wing.
e: False. Air is faster over the longer top of the wing and slower under the bottom, so pressure is lower above. The error is the part about velocity air flow low along top.

q: This causes a low pressure above the wing and a high pressure below the wing which provides a lift on the wing.
e: True. This causes a low pressure above the wing and a high pressure below the wing which provides a lift on the wing. The pressure difference across the wing is the lift.

q: When the piston of the insect sprayer is pressed, the fast moving air causes a low pressure at the tip of the nozzle.
e: True. When the piston of the insect sprayer is pressed, the fast moving air causes a low pressure at the tip of the nozzle. Bernoulli: high speed, low pressure, so the sprayer sucks liquid up the stem.

q: When the piston of the insect sprayer is pressed, the fast moving air causes a high pressure at the tip of the nozzle.
e: False. Fast air at the sprayer nozzle is low pressure, and that drop draws liquid up the stem. The error is the part about piston insect sprayer pressed fast moving.

q: The liquid inside the container of an insect sprayer is at a higher pressure, and therefore rushes up through the stem and out the nozzle.
e: True. The liquid inside the container of an insect sprayer is at a higher pressure, and therefore rushes up through the stem and out the nozzle. The still liquid sits at higher pressure than the fast nozzle air, so it rushes out.

q: The Magnus effect is a particular manifestation of Bernoulli's theorem that is commonly associated with a spinning object moving through a fluid.
e: True. The Magnus effect is a particular manifestation of Bernoulli's theorem that is commonly associated with a spinning object moving through a fluid. Bernoulli's equation keeps p + ½ρv² + ρgh constant along a streamline for incompressible, non-viscous laminar flow.

q: The Magnus effect is commonly associated with a stationary object moving through a vacuum.
e: False. The Magnus effect needs a spinning object moving through a fluid, not a stationary object in vacuum. The error is the part about Magnus effect commonly associated stationary object.

q: In the case of a ball spinning through the air, the turning ball drags some of the air around with it.
e: True. In the case of a ball spinning through the air, the turning ball drags some of the air around with it. That dragged air plus the oncoming stream is the Magnus effect.

q: During cyclones, moving air gains speed above the roof of a house causing the reduced pressure on the roof.
e: True. During cyclones, moving air gains speed above the roof of a house causing the reduced pressure on the roof. Fast cyclone air above the roof drops the outside pressure.

q: During cyclones, moving air gains speed above the roof of a house causing the increased pressure on the roof.
e: False. Faster air above the roof lowers pressure, it does not increase it. The error is the part about cyclones moving air gains speed above.

q: Therefore the pressure inside the house is greater, which can raise the roof.
e: True. Therefore the pressure inside the house is greater, which can raise the roof. Higher indoor pressure than over the roof can lift the roof.

q: Therefore the pressure inside the house is lower, which can raise the roof.
e: False. The inside pressure is then higher than the roof-top pressure, and that difference can lift the roof. The error is the part about Therefore pressure inside house lower raise.
